disputed.why: The coverage ref is wrong and understates the surface. The fragment cites OrganismBehaviorPostureTests.swift:150 approvedLowRiskReflexBiasesPostureWithoutBypassingReview as 'incidental' — I opened that test (lines 150-165) and it does not call toolResultJSON at all. The actual asserting call sites are OrganismBehaviorPostureTests.swift:48, :181 and :249, each of which destructures `posture.toolResultJSON(tool:surface:)` directly. So the core surface IS covered by three asserting tests; the genuine gap the fragment's proposedEval describes is the DISPATCHER-SIDE attachment at Sources/NativeAgentApp/AppChatToolDispatcher.swift:354, which is what the eval should be scoped to.

The proposedEval's premise is already satisfied for half the surface and misses the half that actually leaks. I read SomaticSignalValence.swift:19-66: `canonicalValence` is ALREADY an exhaustive switch with no default — a new SomaticSignalKind cannot compile without a row, so 'assert the switch is exhaustive over allCases' buys nothing. The uncovered hazard is its sibling `adapterSuppressesIntrinsicValence` (:56), which ends in `default: return false` at :63-64 — a new kind silently opts into adapter-stamped valence. Filed as a separate missed surface.

The fragment states the default (non---strict) run exits 0 'no matter how many checks failed', citing script/organism_doctor.sh:265. I did not run the script (it reaches a live bridge and has a --simulate path that mutates the live body), so I could not verify the exit-code behavior empirically. What I did verify from source is adjacent and weaker than claimed for one check: at :226 a MISSING organism_living_status.json is emitted as `status INFO`, not FAIL — so for that particular check the file's absence never reaches FAIL_COUNT at all, meaning even --strict would exit 0 with the iOS body snapshot entirely unpublished. Coverage claim 'smoke / asserts' for the iOS snapshot is therefore too strong.

Dormancy claim confirmed but its date is off by ~5 hours in a way that matters for a dormancy verdict. The fragment says 'last written 2026-07-07 (28KB)'. `ls -la data/cognition/` shows mtime 2026-07-07 17:08, 28,993 bytes — so the direction is right (≈47 days dormant), but I did not open the file's newest line, so 'last WRITTEN' vs 'last mtime-touched' is unverified; the proposedEval it carries (read the newest line's `at` stamp) is exactly the check that would settle it and has not been run.

The `where` folds three distinct public surfaces into one id — frozenRead(at:) at OrganismKernel.swift:378, refreshBodySchemaAndFrozenRead at :173, and frozenRevisionFingerprint() at :445 — and the two cited tests (OrganismBodySchemaTests.swift:285, :362) exercise the first two. I found no test anywhere in Modules/NativeAgentCore/Tests or tests/ that asserts anything about frozenRevisionFingerprint()'s stability or collision behavior, so that third surface's coverage is claimed by association rather than by evidence. A fingerprint that silently stops changing would make every downstream cache-keyed-on-revision serve a stale body.

disputed.why: The silent-failure claim is wrong on its premise. It says 'proposals accumulate pending forever when no drain runs (see memory.promoter.autoAcceptSweep, which has no production caller)'. autoAcceptSweep IS dead — I re-verified: the only hits repo-wide are MemoryV2+AdaptivePromoter.swift:251 and AdaptivePromoterTests.swift:258/:358 — but it is not the drain. MemoryConsolidator is: MemoryV2+Consolidator.swift:163 lists pending proposals and resolves them via rejectProposal (:174, :188), acceptProposal (:208) and markProposalStatus (:299), and it is wired in production through Sources/NativeAgentApp/MemoryConsolidationHygieneRunner.swift. The live store agrees: 355 rejected / 37 accepted / 2 pending. A backlog is not the failure mode here; the real unobserved risk on this surface is staging DORMANCY (newest staged_at 2026-08-20 vs newest memory 2026-08-22), which the fragment's own memory.promoter.threshold proposedEval targets and this surface's narrative contradicts.

Two problems. (1) The silent-failure claim 'if GC never runs, orphan entities accumulate … and nothing reports the orphan ratio' rests on GC being dormant; it is not. Two production callers, both opened: Sources/NativeAgentApp/MemoryConsolidationHygieneRunner.swift:152 (apply:true, approvedOverThreshold:true, on the approved hygiene cadence — its own comment at :141-:151 says it was moved onto that cadence in a 2026-07-21 audit precisely because it used to be dormant) and Sources/NativeAgentApp/KnowledgeGraphView+Maintenance.swift:96/:126 (a manual dry-run + apply UI control the fragment lists as no surface at all). (2) The proposedEval would misdiagnose the live root: I measured 57 relationship-less entities but 783 with NO created_by_indexer stamp, which GC is forbidden to sweep by its own rule (KnowledgeGraphHygieneTests.swift:637). An orphan-ratio lead would read 'GC dormant' when the truth is 'GC ran and is structurally barred from 59% of the graph'. The honest metric is the field GC already computes and both production callers discard — KnowledgeGraphGCReport.legacyUntrackedEntities (KnowledgeGraph+GC.swift:68), filed as a missed surface above.

The coverage refs check out (EmbeddingTests.swift:367, StorageTests.swift:384/:439), but the surface is characterized as a live paraphrase-blocking gate and that is not observably true on User's root: 334 of 386 tombstones have embedding IS NULL, and matchesTombstone (MemoryV2+Storage.swift:2002) only sees rows WHERE embedding IS NOT NULL AND embedding_epoch = active, so 86.5% of the denylist is exact-hash-only. All three coverage refs are hermetic tests over rows the test itself embedded; none reads the live corpus, and no eval at any tier reports gate coverage. Filed separately as memory.tombstone.semanticGateCoverage. Worth recording that I chased and CLEARED the obvious suspect: the app write paths are fine — MemoryV2+Storage.rejectProposal:1844 carries the proposal's embedding (all 394 live proposals have one), deleteMemory:1255 carries the row's embedding, and the Wiring:1049 protocol path that re-writes the same hash embedding-less is saved by upsertTombstone's COALESCE at :1978-:1981, which is exactly what StorageTests:439 pins. The 334 gap came from an out-of-band 2026-08-14 script using the addTombstone(content:reason:) overload, which no eval constrains.

Coverage refs verified, but the claim 'the ONLY external tell is the KG-index-coverage ratio in SYS-05' is wrong for two of the three hooks. The Spotlight hook has a second external tell the fragment lists nowhere: the data/memory/.spotlight_reindexed sentinel, written by Sources/NativeAgentApp/BackgroundLoopsManagerComposition.swift:339 and read by two UI surfaces — Sources/NativeAgentApp/MemoryView.swift:700 and KnowledgeGraphStatusHeader.swift:41 (65 bytes, dated 2026-08-22 on the live root). The USER.md hook's tell is that file's own mtime. Only the KG hook is genuinely down to the index ratio.

I built and RAN it (see ranRun): `swift build --product ContextSelectionABHarness` succeeds, and the binary runs clean against a .backup copy of the live store — exit 0, generation 2576, 546 atoms / 307 sources, 60 queries evaluated / 0 skipped, mandatoryDivergences [], mandatorySetIdenticalAcrossVariants true, and the three variants produce materially different numbers (meanJaccard 0.3985 / 0.2230 / 0.1854), so the weight seam is live. Disputing one implication a reader would draw from the numbers: maximumCandidates=256 sits below the live corpus (my harness run reports 546 atoms in active generation 2576), which invites the conclusion that half the corpus is cut before ranking. disputed.why: The stated silent-failure — 'listActive/listHistory are what DeskView and RunsView render; a status-set drift silently drops rows out of both lists' — is FALSE, and I verified it two ways. (1) `grep -rn 'listActive|listHistory' Sources` returns exactly two hits, both inside a COMMENT at Sources/NativeAgentApp/DeskView.swift:369-372 explaining why DeskView deliberately does NOT use them: 'One listAll() scan, sliced client-side — the runner's listActive/listHistory whitelists would make an unknown/corrupt status (e.g. a future "retrying") vanish from BOTH sections.' The actual read is `await runner.listAll()` at DeskView.swift:2086. (2) No other app file calls either method. So listActive (Runner.swift:1102) and listHistory (Runner.swift:1110) have zero app consumers — they are protocol-level API, and the whitelist hazard the fragment names is the reason the UI avoids them, not a live exposure. Separately, the two cited coverage refs do not touch list partitioning at all: :422 timelineJSONLContainsEnqueuedEvent asserts a timeline event and :546 workshopExecutionRecordToJSONHasAllPythonFields asserts wire-shape parity. The tests that DO exercise the partitions are SwiftNativeWorkshopRunnerTests.swift:1423 (listAll), :1436 (listActive), :1452 (listHistory), none of which the fragment cites. The surface is real; the consumer claim and the coverage refs are both wrong.

The single coverage ref is `script/timer_inventory.tsv:46 ... via script/check_timer_inventory.swift` at strength 'asserts'. I opened both. Line 46 of the TSV is `Modules/NativeAgentCore/Sources/WorkshopExecution/WorkshopExecution+Executor.swift\t*\t2\ttimeout_retry_deadline\tWorkshopStepCancellationDeadline`, and the header row is `# path\tneedle\texpected_count\tclassification\tcanonical_owner`. script/check_timer_inventory.swift:152-156 throws ONLY on `counts[index] != rule.expectedCount` — i.e. the check asserts 'this file contains exactly 2 timer/sleep sites owned by WorkshopStepCancellationDeadline'. It never reads the constant's VALUE, never compares defaultStepTimeoutSeconds() against drainPassTimeoutSeconds, and never verifies the stated invariant that this 1800 matches WorkshopExecutorDrainRunner.tickTimeoutOverride. Raise the step timeout above the pass timeout and the count stays 2, so the check stays green — which is exactly the regression the fragment's own silentFailureMode describes. Strength should be 'incidental'; the surface is effectively uncovered and the fragment's own proposedEval is the right fix.

Declared kind 'env' (NATIVE_AGENT_MAX_ACTIVE_EXECUTIONS, default 3) with one coverage ref at WorkshopExecutorTests.swift:846 slotCapRecheckInsideClaimLockRefusesWhenFull, strength 'asserts'. I read that test (:845-893): it constructs `WorkshopExecutorLoop(root:, llmStep:, maxActive: 1, cancellationPollInterval: 0.02)` — the cap is INJECTED. `defaultMaxActive()` (Executor.swift:390) is never invoked and the env var is never set, unset, or read anywhere in the test. The test proves the claim-lock recheck honours whatever cap it was handed; it proves nothing about the env surface being declared. As with slotsCap, a typo in the canonical string literal at Executor.swift:391 would read the default 3 forever with a fully green suite. Strength should be 'incidental' at the env-surface level, and this surface needs the same env-vocabulary eval the fragment proposed for workshop.runner.slotsCap.

The third coverage ref — 'Modules/NativeAgentCore/Tests/NativeAgentCoreTests/WorkshopWireVocabularyTests.swift NATIVE_AGENT_MAX_ACTIVE vocabulary bridge', strength 'asserts' — does not cover the surface as described. I opened it: WorkshopWireVocabularyTests.swift:111-135 calls the vocabulary helper with an explicitly INJECTED `environment:` dictionary and its own inline string literals ('NATIVE_AGENT_MAX_ACTIVE_EXECUTIONS' / 'NATIVE_AGENT_MAX_ACTIVE_MISSIONS'). Because the test re-declares the literals rather than importing them from the read site, a typo at Runner.swift:206 cannot fail it — which is precisely the failure the fragment names in its own silentFailureMode ('a typo'd canonical name would read the default 3+32 forever and no test goes red'). Coverage ref WorkshopExecutorTests.swift:1842 defaultDeadlineDoesNotAffectFastStep is listed at strength 'asserts'. It does exercise the no-override path, but it only asserts that a fast step reaches `completed` — it pins neither the backstop value nor the env key, so it cannot fail on a renamed variable or a changed default. Worth flagging alongside it: that test's own inline comment reads `// no stepTimeoutInterval → default 3600s; never fires on a fast step` (WorkshopExecutorTests.swift:1852) while defaultStepTimeoutSeconds() returns 1500 (WorkshopExecution+Executor.swift:411). The comment is stale by 2100 seconds and the test passes under either value, which is how the drift survived. Strength should be 'reports-only'; the fragment's proposed env-vocabulary eval is the right fix and should additionally pin the numeric backstop so the comment cannot drift again.

disputed.why: The stated silent-failure mode — 'a caller asking for 200 repos gets the cap with no truncated marker' — is factually wrong. GitHubConnectorActions.swift:66 emits `resultsTruncated: .bool(projection.truncated)` alongside `count` and `sourcePageCount`. The REAL silent failure is narrower and worth restating: `truncated` is computed as sourceCount > rows.count inside projectCollection (GitHubToolProjection.swift:188-189), i.e. it flags PAGE-level truncation only. The `limit` clamp at GitHubConnectorActions.swift:44 silently reduces a requested 200 to 20 BEFORE the request is sent (per_page = 20), so sourceCount is 20, rows.count is 20, and resultsTruncated reads FALSE on exactly the case the fragment worried about. The marker exists; it just cannot see request-level clamping.

One of the two coverage refs is misattributed. `githubRepositoryEntryProjectionIsCompactAndBounded` (Tests/GitHubConnectorTests/GitHubConnectorTests.swift:136) exercises GitHubToolProjection.repositoryEntries, which does NOT route through projectCollection and is called with limit 100 — the test asserts `projected.rows.count == 100`, which proves collectionLimit (20) is NOT applied on that path. The surface IS genuinely covered, but only by the second ref: githubSearchProjectionBoundsRowsBodiesAndNestedPayloads (:324) asserts rows.count == 20 with limit 100, and githubActivityProjectionBoundsEveryCollectionAndExcerpt (:355) does the same for comments. A merge that keeps the first ref will credit the 20-cap to a test that demonstrates a 100-row result.

disputed.why: The smoke coverage claim is VACUOUS — wrong module. The fragment credits `script/smoke_all.sh:36-46` (chat-drive dispatch get_persona_doc / list_skills / recall_memory) as an `asserts`-strength smoke tier for `SwiftNativeDispatcher.dispatch`. I opened the CLI: `Modules/NativeAgentCore/Sources/ChatDrive/main.swift:283-295` — `runDispatch` constructs `SwiftToolDispatcher()` (ChatOrchestration) and calls `d.dispatch(tool:input:surface:)`. That is a DIFFERENT type in a DIFFERENT module with a different signature (no DispatchContext, no dryRun); the file's own header at main.swift:2 says so: "call SwiftToolDispatcher directly". Nothing in smoke_all.sh ever constructs a Dispatcher-module dispatcher. Net effect: the fence's only claimed non-unit-test coverage for its central entry point does not exercise it at all — and this is exactly why the first worker found ZERO kind=="dispatch" rows in the live feed while smoke stayed green. Also note the surface's `writes: [data/traces/events.jsonl]` is production-accurate but unverifiable from any eval, since makeDispatcher's two production call sites pass no ledger and DispatchLedger.tail has no production reader.

Coverage is real but PRODUCTION-INERT — the asserted property cannot occur in the live app. `listServersTTL` guards `_serversCacheRow`/`_inflightListServers`, which are actor-INSTANCE properties (MCPDispatcher.swift:436-444), and every production call site builds a fresh actor: `SwiftNativeMCPDispatcher(root:)` at Sources/NativeAgentApp/NativeClient+MCP.swift:215,309,316,322 and `makeMCPDispatcher()` at :390 (which itself constructs a new instance, MCPDispatcher.swift:1010-1012). So the two cited tests (`listServers_cachesWithinTTL_singleDiskRead` MCPSubprocessClientTests.swift:1546, `listServers_coldConcurrent_singleDiskRead` :1676) hold ONE dispatcher across two calls — a shape production never has. The stated silent-failure mode ("a server added in the hub can take up to 60s to appear") is therefore backwards: the cache never hits across UI calls, so the real live behavior is a disk read per call, and the TTL is a setting with no production effect. Contrast MCPLiveCache.shared (MCPSubprocess+LiveCache.swift:20) and sharedPool (:624), which ARE process-global and do persist — so mcp.liveCache.ttl's coverage claim is sound while this one is not.

One of the four coverage refs is weaker than labeled. The three PoolIdleReapTests refs are genuine behavioral asserts and I verified they exist. The fourth — `script/timer_inventory.tsv:15` asserted by `script/check_timer_inventory.swift:152` — is marked strength `asserts`, but I read the row: `Modules/.../MCPSubprocess+Pool.swift  *  1  event_deadline  MCPSubprocessPool.idleDeadline`. The check asserts a COUNT of timer-shaped needles in the file against an expected integer; it proves a timer is DECLARED and owned, not that the reap fires, that the deadline is armed, or that a child is ever killed. It is a declaration inventory, i.e. reports-only with respect to the loop's behavior. Same over-labeling applies to the identical smoke refs on mcp.subprocess.request (tsv:16), mcp.http.transport (tsv:14), dispatcher.tools.git (tsv:13) and toolexec.runSandbox (tsv:44) — all five rows exist as claimed, none of them asserts loop behavior.

The surface is real but its production reachability is misstated by omission — 5 of the 14 named tools are unreachable in the live app. `.fileSystemDefault` (LocalConnectorActions.swift:97) registers 14 actions including write_file/grep/git_status/git_diff/git_log/repo_dirty_summary, and the fragment's silent-failure story treats them as live. Neither production seam wires that registry: Sources/NativeAgentApp/NativeClient+NativeActions.swift:207-213 and NativeClient+SwiftRuntime.swift:98-104 both merge ONLY the seven read-only scoped registries (personaReadOnly, workspaceListReadOnly, timeNowReadOnly, personaListSkillsReadOnly, readFileReadOnly, fileExcerptReadOnly, systemInfoReadOnly). write_file additionally could not run even if wired, because makeDispatcher strips side-effecting names when autonomyResolver is nil (Dispatcher.swift:1119-1136) and both seams pass nil. So `registryKnowsTheFiveActions` / `registryNowKnowsTenActions` / `registryKnowsWave34Actions` assert the CONTENTS of a registry that production never instantiates — real tests, but they pin a shape, not a live path. The module's own header comments still assert the opposite state (LocalConnectorActions.swift:15-16 "NOTHING wires this into a production caller"; :10-11 "falls back to the existing DORMANT-PROXY HTTP path"), both now false, which is how the misreading survives.

So the exact defect the fragment names (Sweep R4 C16: a caller omits isStreaming and a running tool group renders as a finished summary) has NO coverage at all; this surface should read coverage:[] with the C16 regression as its uncovered silent-failure mode.

SessionDragSourceView.swift:99/109/121 all use NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents (leftMouseDown / leftMouseDragged / leftMouseUp), not addGlobalMonitorForEvents, and each handler is additionally fenced by `event.window === win`. The leak is real (three app-local monitors per row, teardown only via teardownMonitors/dismantleNSView at :95) but its blast radius is this app's windows, not system-wide input; the eval should count install/remove balance across LazyVStack recycles rather than looking for global-monitor symptoms.

DeskInteractionTests.swift:186-205 exercises 4 of the 9 DeskRef kinds (ghPr, url, file, commit-with-repo, commit-without-repo). ghIssue, agent, approval, trace and note — five branches that build labels and copy text, and one that builds a github.com/issues URL by string concat (DeskInteraction.swift:452-455) — are unasserted. The proposed eval is not buildable as written. It says to read 'the dispatcher's surface registry (the same list ProviderRouting pins)' and assert 'a nonsense value fails' — there is no such registry. `surface` is a free String threaded through dispatch and compared ad hoc at the consumers (ChatOrchestrationClient+DispatchWrappers.swift:335, AppModel+ViewClientOps.swift:153/155, AgentBridgeCompletionRouter.swift:603 `surface == "slack"`, NativeClient+ApprovalExecutors.swift:1336). Nothing validates or rejects a surface string, so the surface is real but the eval must instead assert that "desk" is a value at least one gate/telemetry consumer branches on.

Matching is ANY-of (user_mode_eval.swift:1421), so that route can only fail. Nothing covers the Desk segment or that switching segments changes the rendered view.

Strength should be 'reports-only', not 'asserts', for THIS surface. agent_instrument.swift:2670/2688 do register workshop/github_command/{ops.jsonl,github_command_state.json} (verified, and the path matches GitHubCommandStore.swift:667 — same subject), but on the live root the directory does not exist, so the organ reports absent-expected and the instrument makes no claim about the DESK lane's rendering: it cannot tell 'watcher quiet' from 'lane never wired', which is the failure mode the fragment itself names. The desk-side distinction is uncovered.

disputed.why: The stated mechanism is wrong. The fragment says "two-writer drift — Settings owns @AppStorage(\"organismKernelEnabled\") while this toggle calls the runtime directly; the two can disagree with no visible conflict." They cannot diverge that way: NativeCognitionRuntime writes the SAME UserDefaults key the @AppStorage observes — NativeCognitionRuntime.swift:1810 `static let organismKernelEnabledKey = "organismKernelEnabled"`, written at NativeCognitionRuntime+Organism.swift:158 and NativeCognitionRuntime.swift:1391/:1769, read back at :1732/:1753; SlimSettingsView.swift:318 declares the @AppStorage over that same key. One key, two writers, and @AppStorage observes the store, so the Settings switch follows the runtime write. The real residual risk is ORDERING (the observatory binding mutates local @State first and fires the runtime write in a detached Task at CognitionObservatoryView.swift:316-321, and refresh() re-reads `next.organism.enabled` rather than the defaults key) — a different failure, and the proposed eval as written would pass while proving nothing about it.

disputed.why: The stated silent-failure mode is factually wrong and the proposed eval would pass vacuously. The fragment says "the string is not rendered anywhere in ProviderSettingsView's body (unlike ToolsView which flashes it). A failed per-surface save is therefore invisible." It IS rendered: Sources/NativeAgentApp/ProviderSettingsView.swift:326-328 — `if !statusText.isEmpty { Text(statusText).font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.secondary).textSelection(.enabled) }` — in the page body just above `.navigationTitle("Providers")` at :335. The config sheet's own statusText (:938) is likewise rendered at :1084-1086. The proposed eval ("the statusText state is rendered by at least one Text/label in the view body") therefore asserts something already true and can never fail. The real weakness here is different and unstated: statusText is never cleared and never timestamped, so a save error from ten minutes ago sits under the picker column reading as current — that is the honest eval to write.

The surface is real and its CORE claim verified by me — data/providers/active.json and surfaces.json each carry 17 keys including `cognition_cue`; MODEL_SURFACES (Modules/NativeAgentCore/Sources/ProviderRouting/ProviderRouting.swift:310-313) lists 16 and does not include it; grep finds cognition_cue only in docs/build_plans/fable5-consciousness-wave1.md:79 and iOS/NativeAgentMobile/Tests/UIIntegrityContractTests.swift:26. But the cited evidence is wrong: the fragment says "the file comment records this already happened once (\"rem\" was missing)". It does not. `rem` IS in MODEL_SURFACES (:311). The comment at ProviderRouting.swift:307-309 names `self_improvement` as the surface that was called but absent from the registry and "silently fell through to the chat pin — unpinnable and invisible in Providers", added 2026-08-21; the other comment (:302-306) is about the missions→workshop rename. Worth noting the iOS side already has the pin this fence lacks (UIIntegrityContractTests.swift:26 asserts the picker list does NOT contain cognition_cue), so the Mac fence is the uncovered half of an invariant iOS tests.

Not disputed as a surface, but the proposed eval as written cannot pass and would be discarded as broken on first run. It asserts "every entry maps to a label that is not the raw id and contains no underscore" over MODEL_SURFACES — but MODEL_SURFACES contains `rem`, whose natural label is "REM", a raw-id match under any case-insensitive comparison, and the assertion gives no acronym rule. The honest form: every MODEL_SURFACES entry hits a NAMED case in the switch at ProviderSettingsView.swift:754 (none reaches the `surface.capitalized` default), mutation-provable by adding an entry and requiring failure.

Declared fully covered ("n/a — covered", costSeconds 0) on the strength of two FirstRunProviderReadinessTests cases. Those pin the two directions of the VERDICT (a pass clears unverified; a provider with no live probe is not marked failed), but nothing pins the button's liveness: runTest at ProviderSettingsView.swift:1169 is an async Task whose only state is the sheet's statusText (:1178/:1181), with no deadline. A probe that hangs leaves the sheet with no result and no error indefinitely — the same unbounded-wait class the fragment itself flags for chatgptOAuthButton and anthropicOAuthDirectPanel but exempts here. Marking it closed hides a live gap.

Marked "well covered by fail-closed validation tests", costSeconds 0. The four TrustBackupRestoreSafetyTests cases cover validation and the safety-backup path, but the surface as the fragment itself describes it ("writes: the entire data root (replaced)") has a second half nobody pins: what happens AFTER a successful restore. Every in-memory subsystem — provider pins, trust policy, chat sessions, embeddings status — was loaded from the OLD root and is not invalidated by the file replacement. A restore that succeeds on disk while the running process keeps serving pre-restore state is a stale-UI failure with no test, and it is invisible precisely because every validation test passes. Not disputed as a surface; disputed as closed.

Modules/NativeAgentCore/Tests/ActivityWatchTests/ActivityQueryTests.swift:11 is titled "QUERY PRIVACY: capture consent does not imply model access consent" and drives allowModelAccess through the query path (see also :26 constructing a policy with allowModelAccess: true). The honest gap is narrower than the fragment states: what is uncovered is the CHAT answer path's consultation of the flag, not the query gate itself. The proposed eval should be re-scoped to the chat/tool call site, not written from scratch.

Coverage is claimed EMPTY, but the proposed eval's exact property is already pinned. Modules/NativeAgentCore/Tests/ActivityWatchTests/ActivitySpanEngineTests.swift:439 "TITLES: browser titles need BOTH captureTitles and browserTitlesEnabled" walks the flag combinations and, at :456-459 under the comment "appNameOnlyMode overrides everything", asserts allowsTitleCapture is false for both a browser and a non-browser bundle with appNameOnly true. :378 pins titles-off-by-default and :461 pins that a browser with titles disabled still records duration. What remains genuinely uncovered is only the VIEW's disable-wiring (that appNameOnlyMode greys the other two switches at :186/:212), not the policy semantics.

The coverage list cites only the consent test (wipe-before-capture creates no store) and the silentFailureMode is presented as a hypothesis about runRetention never being scheduled. Both halves need correcting. The runner IS covered — Modules/NativeAgentCore/Tests/ActivityWatchTests/ActivityPolicyAndRetentionTests.swift:154 (prunes past the window), :182 (durable across processes, not re-run early), :201 (backwards clock makes it due), :215 (nothing left in the WAL sidecar). And the hypothesis is not a hypothesis: I confirmed by grep (see ranRun) that the app has exactly ONE caller of runRetention() — setRetentionDays at ActivityWatchController.swift:236 — with no launch or periodic call site, and that runRetention early-returns on a nil spanStore. The clone-tier eval the fragment proposes would re-test the already-green runner; the real missing eval is a call-site/reachability check, which I filed as loop.activityRetentionSweep.

The coverage claim is factually wrong about what these buttons use. It cites SystemPermissionPreflightTests:171 as covering "the shared anchor vocabulary these buttons build on" — they build on nothing shared. MacControlPermissionsView.swift:447/:452/:457 hardcode the LEGACY macOS-12 prefix `x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?…`, while the shared builder SystemPermissionPreflight.swift:116 and MacIntegrationView.swift:421/:667 use the macOS-13+ prefix `com.apple.settings.PrivacySecurity.extension?`. So the cited test exercises a vocabulary these three buttons never call, and the two panes of the same app disagree about how to deep-link to Privacy & Security. Coverage for this surface should be recorded as EMPTY, and the divergence itself is a finding.

The proposed eval is not runnable as written and the surface is anchored at the wrong boundary. HealthPill.label(for:) and color(for:) are declared `private` (HealthPill.swift:58 and :71), so no test can read them across buckets. The testable boundary — and the one carrying the real cold-launch honesty invariant — is `AppModel.systemHealthSummary` (HealthPill.swift:10-21), which the fragment never names as a surface at all. I filed it under missed as public-api.AppModel.systemHealthSummary; this entry's eval should either target that property or be a source-conformance assertion over HealthPill's switch.

It should be graded reports-only/incidental, and the surface should carry a proposedEval (a source-conformance check that the bump call exists on the audited surfaces) rather than being treated as covered.

ICloudSyncStatePaths.stateDirectory (Modules/NativeAgentCore/Sources/PersistenceCore/ICloudSyncStatePaths.swift:15-17) returns `<dataRoot>/icloud`, NOT `<dataRoot>/icloud/state`; snapshotSkips (:51-53) is therefore `data/icloud/snapshot_skips.json`. Confirmed on the live root: `ls -la data/icloud/` shows chat_delivery_receipts.jsonl, processed_ids.json, snapshot_digests.json and the inbox/outbox/responses/snapshots dirs — there is no `state/` subdirectory at all.

Both the directory AND the filename in `writes` are wrong. Per ICloudSyncStatePaths.swift:36-46 the real location is `<dataRoot>/icloud/completed-unarchived/<msgId>.completed-unarchived` (hyphen in the directory name, and the extension is `completed-unarchived`, not `.json`). The fragment says `data/icloud/state/completed_unarchived/<msgId>.json` — wrong on the parent dir, wrong on the underscore-vs-hyphen, wrong on the extension. An eval or instrument reader wired to that path would report 'no unarchived completions' unconditionally, which is exactly the silent-zero the surface exists to catch.

disputed.why: Coverage ref is real (UIIntegrityContractTests.swift:94 testSkillsAndToolsShareOnePrimaryDestination exists) but strength "asserts" is wrong for the surface as described. That test asserts only that ContentView contains the literal "SkillsToolsView()" and that a specific retired tabItem string is absent (:99-100). It asserts NOTHING about tab COUNT or geometry — which is precisely the named failure mode ("adding a 6th tab pushes one behind iOS overflow with no test catching it"). This surface is effectively uncovered; the right strength is incidental, and the eval it needs (assert the TabView has exactly 5 tab items) does not exist.

Coverage cited as UIIntegrityContractTests.swift:103 "(asserts tools_snapshot.json is read via loadSnapshotArrayAsync)", strength asserts. Line 103 is XCTAssertTrue(combined.contains("tools_snapshot.json")) — a source-string scrape of SkillsToolsView.swift; the loadSnapshotArrayAsync assertion is a separate line (:104) and targets iCloudSyncEngine+Snapshots.swift. Neither executes the store. The named failure mode (nil read + non-empty tools ⇒ silent stale catalog, MobileToolCatalogStore) is completely untested. Strength should be incidental at best.

Cites UIIntegrityContractTests.swift:141 as "asserts". Line 141 is XCTAssertTrue(desk.contains("await sync.refreshDeskSnapshot()")) — it proves a call site is spelled that way in the source, nothing about behavior. The stated silent failure ("refreshDeskSnapshot failing is not surfaced on this screen") is exactly what the assertion cannot see. Strength should be reports-only, and the surface needs a real eval.

Cites UIIntegrityContractTests.swift:143 testSnapshotGroupsDriveVisibleStoresWithoutCloudPolling as "asserts". Line 143 is XCTAssertTrue(memory.contains(".onChange(of: sync.memories)")) — a source scrape proving the view observes the projection. The stated failure mode (importance tint thresholds 0.7/0.4 repainting every memory the same color after a Mac-side scale change) has no assertion anywhere. Strength should be incidental.

Cites ChatStoreMergeTests.swift:249 test_unmatchedLateCancellationCannotStopANewerTurn as "asserts". That test is real and does pin correlation matching on cancellation — but the surface's stated failure mode is a VISIBILITY one ("stop only renders while store.isLoading; if isLoading goes false while the Mac turn is still live the user has no cancel"). No test covers the render gate. The coverage is for a different property than the one at risk; strength should be incidental.

Not a coverage dispute — a factual correction. The silentFailureMode says the badge is "a max() of five independent sources". Read at ContentView.swift:41-58 it is a SUM of five buckets, two of which are internally max()'d pairs (approvalsStore.pendingCount vs the sync.approvals filter; inboxStore.activeCount vs the sync.inboxItems filter). The proposedEval ("the badge equals the sum across all five buckets") is correct and should be kept; the description would mislead whoever implements it into asserting the wrong operator.

I opened iOS/NativeAgentMobile/Tests/UIIntegrityContractTests.swift:107-119: the test is a pure source-TEXT grep — XCTAssertTrue(bridge.contains("NAMobileSnapshotGroup.allCases")) plus four other string containment checks. It never constructs a transport, never registers an observer, and asserts nothing about the four observe* Tasks at iCloudBridge.swift:359-387. Real output: (H) app side closes the socket -> relay exits rc=0, stderr empty, and the frame Chrome then wrote is lost (parent got BrokenPipeError because the relay was already gone); (I) Chrome's end of the relay's stdout closed, app writes a valid framed response -> rc = -13, i.e. death by SIGPIPE, stderr EMPTY — the diagnostic/EXIT_FAILURE path at main.swift:169-170 never runs; (J) 1 MiB+8 frame -> rc=1 `[NativeAgentChromeRelay] Native-messaging frame is 1048584 bytes; maximum is 1048576.` and the WHOLE process dies on one oversize message; (K) three sequential Chrome->app frames all forwarded byte-exact, rc=0; (L) app writes {"pending":true} then stdin closes -> relay exits rc=0 having delivered NOTHING to stdout (empirical confirmation of the first worker's inferred teardown-drop). A sibling run (relay_probe.py, same session) additionally confirmed: valid object round-trips both directions; `[]` -> rc=1 topLevelJSONMustBeObject; `{` -> rc=1 invalidJSON; missing listener -> rc=1 errno 2; relative path -> rc=1 'must be absolute'; 200-char path -> rc=1 'exceeds the Unix-socket limit'. So the binary is CORRECT today — the gap is purely that no eval in the repo executes it.

(1) The cited ref — 'Modules/NativeAgentCore/Sources/PersistenceCore/TurnTrace.swift:632 names AnthropicStreamMessagesSSETests thinking tests as the shared-bus subscribers' — is a SOURCE COMMENT about persist-lane root redirection, not a test and not coverage. So the fragment's proposedEval ('a reachability proof, hermetic, 5s') already ships. (3) The stated failure mode is wrong: 'Either the OAuth-direct adapter is not the live path or the emit is unreachable' is not the explanation. The emit is gated on InspectorThinkingLane.summarizedThinking, a @TaskLocal that defaults FALSE and is bound only when the persisted UserDefaults key inspectorThinkingSummarized is on AND surface == "chat" (TurnTraceW2.swift:111-134; adapter guard at LLMClient+AnthropicOAuthDirectAdapter.swift:207; bind at ChatOrchestration+Streaming.swift:486/:619). Could not verify the coverage ref, and the described resolution order is incomplete. Modules/NativeAgentCore/Tests/PersistenceCoreTests/TurnTraceW2Tests.swift at the cited line 116 is inside a prose comment block ('The shared-bus tests pollute the live turn_traces feed unless the persist lane can be redirected...'), not a test. The tests that actually assert the ordering begin a few lines later (resolveRoot_env_outranks_everything and siblings) and — per that same comment — they test the PURE resolveRoot helper and deliberately never mutate the process-wide static, so they do not cover the live-lane behaviour the surface describes. disputed.why: The stated silent-failure mode is empirically FALSE. The fragment claims "Env assignments precede a shell FUNCTION call (`NATIVEAGENT_RANGE_BENCH_LIVE=1 ... step ...`); in bash these persist in the shell after the call rather than being scoped to it, so the live-bench env leaks into any later step." I ran the exact construct: `bash -c 'f(){ echo "in=[${V:-unset}]"; }; V=1 f; echo "after=[${V:-unset}]"'` → `in=[1]` / `after=[unset]`. Bash only makes function-preceding assignments persist in POSIX mode (`set -o posix`); script/evals.sh:7 sets `set -uo pipefail` and never enables posix, so the assignment IS scoped to the call. The FLAG is a real surface — keep it — but its proposed eval ("assert NATIVEAGENT_RANGE_BENCH_LIVE is not set in the environment of any subsequent step") would pass vacuously today and pins a property that is not at risk. The genuine risk on that line is different and unstated: `[ "$LIVE" = 1 ] && ... step ...` under `set -uo pipefail` (no -e) means a step whose own guard errors contributes nothing to `fails`.

It cites "tests/scripts/github_release_updater_test.sh:6 (consumed via NATIVEAGENT_PUBLISH_TEST_RECEIPT in script/publish_github_release.sh)" as `asserts` for the RECEIPT SURFACE.
